input.reason: The reported race is real. In compactHeadViewLocked, the watermark comes from `iso.lastAppendID()`. That function returns the most recent append ID handed out, including IDs held by appenders that are still open. In upstream Prometheus, an appender gets its append ID when it is created, and its samples are stamped with that ID when it commits. (head_append.go is missing from this checkout, so that part is based on upstream code.) So if an appender with ID N opens before the watermark is taken and commits after the block is written, its samples are not in the block but are recorded with ID N in s.txs. `hasAppendIDAbove(s, N)` checks `N > N`, which is false, so the series is evicted and tombstoned in the WAL. The committed sample is then lost, both from the head and on WAL replay. This is exactly the late-append data loss the guard was added to prevent; it only catches appenders created after the watermark.

structured_output.reason: The reported race is real. In compactHeadViewLocked, the watermark comes from `iso.lastAppendID()`. That function returns the most recent append ID handed out, including IDs held by appenders that are still open. In upstream Prometheus, an appender gets its append ID when it is created, and its samples are stamped with that ID when it commits. (head_append.go is missing from this checkout, so that part is based on upstream code.) So if an appender with ID N opens before the watermark is taken and commits after the block is written, its samples are not in the block but are recorded with ID N in s.txs. `hasAppendIDAbove(s, N)` checks `N > N`, which is false, so the series is evicted and tombstoned in the WAL. The committed sample is then lost, both from the head and on WAL replay. This is exactly the late-append data loss the guard was added to prevent; it only catches appenders created after the watermark.
